q: Figure 05-A: What is Figure A?
n: In Figure A the deflector sits above the frame, the mark of an upright sprinkler, installed pointing up from exposed piping. Source: NFPA 13 (sprinkler types).

q: Figure 05-A: What is Figure B?
n: Figure B is a smoke detector, which senses smoke particles and signals the fire alarm panel. Source: NFPA 72.

q: Figure 05-A: What is Figure C?
n: Figure C is a Siamese (fire department) connection, a twin-inlet fitting through which fire trucks pump water into the standpipe or sprinkler system. Source: NFPA 14; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: What is Figure D?
n: Figure D is a fire pump set, which supplies the water flow and pressure that fire protection systems need. Source: NFPA 20 (stationary fire pumps).

q: Figure 05-A: What is Figure E?
n: Figure E is a portable fire extinguisher. Portable extinguishers are rated by fire class (A, B, C, D, K) and must be mounted visibly and within reach along exit paths. Source: NFPA 10; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: Which pump lifts water from an underground cistern to an overhead tank?
n: A transfer pump lifts water from the underground cistern to the elevated (overhead) tank. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (water supply systems).

q: Which pump keeps the sprinkler piping pressurized?
n: A jockey (pressure maintenance) pump keeps the sprinkler piping at pressure by making up small leaks, so the main fire pump does not start unnecessarily. Source: NFPA 20.

q: Which pump raises water pressure when supply pressure is too low?
n: A booster pump raises water pressure when the supply pressure is too low for the fixtures or upper floors. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines; ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: Which pump uses a spinning impeller to move and pressurize water?
n: A centrifugal pump uses a spinning impeller to throw water outward, converting the energy into flow and pressure. Source: Hydraulic Institute standards; ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: Which pump is installed in an elevator pit?
n: A sump pump is installed in the elevator pit to remove water that seeps or drains in, as elevator codes require. Source: ASME A17.1 / Philippine Elevator Code (pit drainage).

q: Which fire suppression system is commonly used in parking garages?
n: Parking garages are commonly protected by wet-pipe sprinklers in the frost-free Philippines, since there is no freezing risk that would call for dry pipe. Source: NFPA 13; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: Which sprinkler system keeps pressurized air or nitrogen in the pipes until it activates?
n: A dry-pipe system keeps pressurized air or nitrogen in the pipes, and water enters only when a sprinkler opens and the dry valve trips. Source: NFPA 13.

q: Which system floods an area with water at once through open heads?
n: A deluge system has open heads, so when the deluge valve opens all heads discharge at once and flood the area. Source: NFPA 13 / NFPA 15.

q: Which system suits places where accidental discharge must be avoided, like museums?
n: A pre-action system fills with water only after a detection system confirms fire, guarding against accidental discharge in museums, archives and data rooms. Source: NFPA 13.

q: Which sprinkler system is the most reliable and most widely installed?
n: Wet-pipe systems have water already in the pipes. They are the simplest, most reliable and most widely installed sprinkler type. Source: NFPA 13; NFPA fire experience data.

q: Which equipment controls or suppresses fire over a wide area?
n: A sprinkler system controls or suppresses fire over a wide area automatically, floor by floor. Source: NFPA 13.

q: Which type of building is classified as a light hazard for fire protection?
n: Offices are classified as light hazard occupancies (low fuel load and combustibility) for sprinkler design. Source: NFPA 13, Annex A (occupancy classification).

q: If water damage is a major concern, which type of sprinkler system is recommended?
n: Water mist systems use very fine droplets and little water, so they limit water damage while cooling and smothering fire. Source: NFPA 750 (water mist systems).

q: Which sprinkler system is most suitable for protecting electrical transformers or tanks with flammable liquids?
n: Deluge (open-head) systems drench transformers and flammable-liquid tanks at once, cooling them and preventing the spread of fire. Source: NFPA 15 (water spray fixed systems); NFPA 13.

q: Which standpipe is for firefighters' use only?
n: A dry standpipe has no water until the fire department pumps it in through the Siamese connection, so it is for firefighters' use only. Source: NFPA 14; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: What is the maximum allowable speed of an escalator?
n: Escalator speed is limited to about 0.6 m/s (120 fpm) at maximum. Source: ASME A17.1 / Philippine Elevator and Escalator Code.

q: What is the usual operating speed of an escalator?
n: Escalators commonly run at about 0.5 m/s (90–100 fpm) in normal service. Source: ASME A17.1; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.

q: When choosing the location of an escalator, what is the primary consideration?
n: Escalators are located where crowds concentrate, along the main circulation, to relieve congestion and move people continuously. Source: Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.

q: Which of the following is considered the most economical layout for an escalator?
n: The criss-cross arrangement stacks up and down units in a compact footprint with continuous travel, the most economical escalator layout. Source: Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.

q: What best justifies escalators over elevators?
o: Continuous heavy foot traffic between nearby levels
n: Escalators are justified for continuous heavy foot traffic between nearby levels, as in malls and stations, where they move many more people than elevators. Source: Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.

q: What is the protective device found inside an elevator shaft?
n: The counterweight balances the car and is guided in the shaft, keeping the car under control and reducing the load on the machine and brake. It is part of the hoistway's safety arrangement. Source: ASME A17.1; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.

q: What is a small lift that carries objects, not people?
n: A dumbwaiter is a small lift that carries goods such as food, linen and documents, not people. Source: ASME A17.1 (dumbwaiters); Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.

q: What is the minimum required depth for an elevator pit?
n: Elevator pits need a minimum depth below the lowest landing to house buffers and give refuge space. About 600 mm is quoted as the minimum for small, low-speed lifts. Source: ASME A17.1 / Philippine Elevator Code (pit requirements).

q: For athree-storey building intended as a Senior Citizen Center with limited budget and space, which type of elevator is most appropriate?
n: For a low-rise (three-storey) building on a tight budget, a hydraulic elevator is cheapest, needs no penthouse machine room and gives a smooth, slow ride suited to seniors. Source: Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook; BP 344 IRR (elevators).

q: Which cable feeds power to the elevator car and moves with it?
n: The traveling cable hangs from the car and moves with it, carrying power and signals to the car's lights, controls and door operator. Source: ASME A17.1; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook.
